desc:
Return the start index of every occurrence of pattern inside text, in increasing order. Occurrences may overlap. If pattern does not occur, return an empty array.

Example: text = "aaabaaa" and pattern = "aa" give [0,1,4,5], because "aa" starts at indices 0, 1, 4 and 5.
constraints: Both strings consist of lowercase English letters
pattern may be longer than text, in which case the answer is empty
hints: Checking every start index with a slice comparison is O(n · m) in the worst case. Is that acceptable for these limits? Can it be made linear?
After a full match, you do not have to restart from scratch: the pattern's longest border says how much of the match can be reused for the next, overlapping, occurrence.
Run KMP: build the prefix function of pattern, scan text with a matched-length counter k, record i - m + 1 whenever k == m, and then set k = pi[k-1] to continue.
editorial: Build the prefix function pi of the pattern. Scan the text with a counter k of currently matched pattern characters: on a mismatch fall back with k = pi[k-1], on a match increase k. When k reaches the pattern length m, an occurrence ends at the current index i, so it starts at i - m + 1.
To find the next occurrence, which may overlap this one, continue with k = pi[m-1], the longest border of the pattern. Everything before that is already known to match.

Total work is O(n + m) because k grows by at most one per text character and each fallback lowers it. The same code works as a Z-function approach on pattern + '#' + text, where each value equal to m marks an occurrence.
